summary: AI observability has become one of the most consequential infrastructure decisions for teams running LLMs in production, with 73% of enterprises requiring AI agent monitoring yet 63.4% citing inadequate tooling as a major barrier. These tools provide visibility into traces, costs, latency, prompt performance, and evaluation quality—the difference between teams running production-grade monitoring and those flying blind. As LLM usage scales, observability and cost monitoring directly control spend, reliability, and the ability to debug complex agent behavior.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.monitors: End-to-end traces, inference cost per trace (including tool calls), prompt performance, and LLM/agent evaluation.
features: LangChain/LangGraph-native tracing with deepest framework support
Auto-instrumentation for low-effort setup
Annotation queues and evaluation framework
Agent debugging and step-by-step trace inspection
Cost analytics per trace
tools.pricing: Free tier available; paid from $39/seat/month (seat-based + usage). Approx. £80/month for typical team usage.
tools.best_for: Engineering teams building on LangChain/LangGraph who want rich debugging and a comprehensive evaluation framework.

tools.name: Helicone
tools.monitors: Per-request cost, latency, and token metrics across 100+ models via a proxy.
features: One-line base URL change for instant setup (~2 mins)
Lightweight proxy routing across many models
Best-in-class cost tracking and usage visibility
Self-host or SDK-only options
Minimal maintenance overhead
tools.pricing: Free tier for low usage; paid from ~£20/month (usage/request-based SaaS).
tools.best_for: Lean engineering teams wanting the simplest setup and cheapest, fastest cost visibility. Not built for finance chargeback/procurement workflows.

tools.name: Weights & Biases (W&B)
tools.monitors: Full ML/LLM experiment tracking, model performance, prompt evaluations, and LLM traces (via W&B Weave).
features: Experiment tracking and model versioning
W&B Weave for LLM tracing and evaluation
Dataset and artifact lineage
Rich dashboards and collaboration tools
Integrates across the broader ML lifecycle
tools.pricing: Free tier for individuals/small teams; usage- and seat-based paid plans (enterprise pricing on request).
tools.best_for: Teams that need unified ML experiment tracking alongside LLM observability within a mature MLOps platform.

tools.name: Arize AI (incl. Arize Phoenix)
tools.monitors: Production LLM/ML performance, evaluation, drift, and tracing. Phoenix focuses on open-source evaluation and tracing.
features: Phoenix open-source library for evaluation and tracing
LLM evaluation, drift detection, and troubleshooting
OpenTelemetry-based instrumentation
Embedding and RAG analysis
Usage-based cost and pricing dimensions
tools.pricing: Phoenix is free/open-source; Arize AX offers free tier with usage-based paid enterprise plans.
tools.best_for: Mid-size and enterprise teams wanting deep evaluation and drift monitoring, with Phoenix as a no-lock-in open-source option.

tools.name: LangFuse
tools.monitors: Traces, prompt management, token usage, cost, and evaluation hooks in a single open-source platform.
features: MIT-licensed open-source core with self-host option for data sovereignty
Combined tracing, prompt management, and evaluation
Comprehensive (manual) instrumentation
Cost analytics and usage tracking
Framework-agnostic
tools.pricing: Cloud free tier (<50K events), then ~£20/month for ~500K; self-hosted ~£30/month infra plus ~2hrs/month maintenance.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting an open-source, data-sovereign observability platform with full control, suitable from startups to enterprise self-hosting.

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.monitors: LLM traces, latency, token usage, and costs via OpenTelemetry-based instrumentation.
features: Open-source OpenTelemetry extension for LLM apps
Vendor-neutral—export traces to any OTel-compatible backend (Datadog, New Relic, Grafana, etc.)
SDK instrumentation for popular LLM providers and frameworks
Avoids vendor lock-in by building on open standards
Integrates into existing observability stacks
tools.pricing: Free and open-source; cost depends on the backend you export telemetry to (Traceloop offers a hosted commercial tier).
tools.best_for: Teams that already run OpenTelemetry-based observability (e.g., Datadog, New Relic, Grafana) and want standards-based, lock-in-free LLM instrumentation.

cost_tips: Route requests through a gateway or proxy (e.g., Portkey or Helicone) to enable fallbacks, caching, and per-department cost tracking—cost governance can be set up in under five minutes.
Cache repeated or similar prompts and use prompt/response caching to avoid paying for identical inference calls multiple times.
Match the model to the task: use smaller, cheaper models for simple requests and reserve frontier models for complex reasoning, using routing and load balancing to optimize cost per request.
Monitor token usage per trace and set budgets/alerts so you catch runaway agent loops or oversized context windows before they inflate your bill.
